newsitem.title: USA: US steelmakers' earnings down in Q3 - analysts.
newsitem.headline: US steelmakers' earnings down in Q3 - analysts.

text.p: Lower steel prices should cause U.S. steelmakers to report lower third quarter earnings, but there's a ray of hope that the industry will see higher steel prices in the fourth quarter.

"Prices have been rising since (last December) but on a year-to-year basis (in the third quarter), they're still slightly lower," said Aldo Mazzaferro at C.J. Lawrence/Deutsche Morgen Grenfell. "But the fourth quarter should show price improvement on a year-to-year basis."
Some analysts, however, also are predicting higher import pressure in the fourth quarter.

Analysts are expecting third-quarter earnings at all U.S. integrated steelmakers to be lower than a year before. AK Steel Holding Corp is expected to post the industry's best performance, while Weirton Steel Corp is expected to post one of the worst.
AK Steel should be the first company to report earnings. The company is expected to post earnings October 8 or 9.

Analysts said steel demand is strong but contract prices in supply agreements with large customers, including automakers, have fallen from last year because steelmakers gave in to customers' demands for lower prices.
"Volume's fantastic but these guys are not making reasonable earnings because they gave away the store to contract customers," said Chuck Bradford at UBS Securities.
Mazzaferro said pricing on average is down $10-$15 per short ton this year versus last year.
Bradford said some companies, including Inland Steel Industries Inc, were also hurt by higher operating costs and a less favorable product mix in the third quarter.

Analysts said the industry's collective operating profit per ton, widely considered one of the best measures of steel companies' performance, fell in this year's third quarter as a result of lower earnings.
Mike Gambardella at J.P. Morgan Securities Inc predicted integrated steelmakers will post an average operating profit of $25 per ton in the third quarter, compared with $29 per ton last year.
